title: CSS Modules pattern crashes using [name]
impact: JS/Rust API users who call transform() with cssModules and a [name] pattern but no filename (or a filename with no stem such as '', '/', '..'). Published builds use panic='abort', so the panic kills the whole Node process (exit 134) instead of throwing; nothing catchable. 0 reactions, no duplicates. Maintainer replied in 2023 that filename must be passed; filename is required in node/index.d.ts, so TS users are warned, plain JS users and the docs example (which elides filename as '// ...') are not.
summary: With a [name] segment in cssModules.pattern and no filename, Pattern::write unwraps Path::file_stem() of an empty path and panics. In released npm builds (panic=abort) this aborts the Node process. It should either fall back (e.g. an empty or placeholder name) or return a normal error saying [name] requires a filename.
repro: 516-repro.mjs: transform({cssModules:{pattern:'my-company-[name]-[hash]-[local]'}, code:'.logo{background:skyblue}'}) -> panic 'called Option::unwrap() on a None value' at css_modules.rs:161. 516-repro-filename.mjs: same with filename 'src/logo.module.css' -> .my-company-logo-module-0Bc8-q-logo (works). 516-repro-edge.mjs: filenames '', '/', '..' panic; 'dir/', '.css', 'a.module.css' ok.
evidence: scripts/repro.mjs on local (master), 1.21.0 and 1.33.0: all panic. Direct node -e on 1.33.0: process aborted, exit 134, try/catch not reached. Local debug build throws a catchable JS error instead (debug profile unwinds), so master and releases look different but have the same bug.

fix.approach: Replace the unwraps in Segment::Name with a fallible path: either return an error (e.g. a new CSS modules error 'the [name] pattern segment requires a filename') or fall back to an empty string; add tests in src/lib.rs next to the existing css_modules pattern tests. Maintainer should pick error vs fallback; an error is more in line with 'strict by default'. Pattern::write's generic error type may need a small plumbing change if erroring.

draftReply:
Thanks for the report, and sorry for the slow follow-up. This still happens on the latest release (1.33.0): with `[name]` in `cssModules.pattern` and no `filename` option, Lightning CSS panics, and in the published builds that aborts the Node process rather than throwing an error you can catch. The workaround is to pass `filename` to `transform()` (it is what `[name]` is derived from), e.g. `filename: 'src/logo.module.css'` gives `.my-company-logo-module-...-logo`. A missing filename should produce a clear error instead of a crash, so I'm leaving this open as a bug.
